Perfect! The main line is:
1. e4 (discovers attack on bishop, attacks knight) Bxc1 (best try)
2. Rxc1+ (wins the bishop) Nc3+ (best try to create complications)
3. Rxc3+ (wins the knight for free)

We end up +3 (bishop) + 3 (knight) - 3 (our bishop) = +3 material net gain. Actually wait, let me recalculate: we started by sacrificing our bishop to win their bishop (net 0), then we won their knight (net +3). So we're up a knight.

This is clearly the best move: **e4** discovers a powerful attack on the bishop and simultaneously attacks the knight.

**Best move:** e4

**Main line:** e4 Bxc1 Rxc1+ Nc3+ Rxc3+ Kd8 (or Kb8/Kd7)

**Motif:** discoveredAttack

**Explanation:**
The pawn move e4 discovers an attack from your bishop on h6 (undefended) while also attacking the knight on d5. Black must deal with both threats but loses material either way. After the forced sequence Bxc1 Rxc1+ Nc3+ Rxc3+, you've won a full knight. Watch for discovered attacks by moving pieces that unmask your own pieces—here the bishop becomes a powerful force.
